name: NJ-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Overwhelming financial edge: Norcross has $2.4M on hand versus about $2,000 for Galdo
D+10 district with a well-entrenched incumbent seeking another term
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 96 percent

model.rationale: Norcross combines a Democratic-leaning district with a roughly 118-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets price his reelection near 96 percent; with no polls or ratings pointing to competition, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: Any late outside spending on Galdo's behalf or surprise polling placing him within single digits would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Donald Norcross enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a South Jersey district that has leaned about ten points Democratic at the presidential level. He has raised more than $1.8 million and holds $2.4 million on hand, while Republican Damon Galdo has raised under $16,000, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters. No public polling of the race is available, and national race raters have not flagged the district as competitive.

Prediction markets give the incumbent roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat, and the fundamentals point the same way: a Democratic-leaning electorate, an entrenched incumbent, and a challenger with negligible resources. Unless Galdo attracts serious outside support or the political environment shifts sharply against Democrats in New Jersey, this seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin.
